pages.title: External CRT Monitor
pages.text: A vintage studio monitor with two uses: beside a radio computer running $(l:radiocraft:computer/wxsat)WXSAT$() it shows the weather satellite mosaic centred where it stands, about 1,000 blocks a tube; on its own touching a premium radio it shows the radio's waterfall.

pages.title: Weather pictures
pages.text: Place it beside the computer, or on its data wire, or beside another monitor that is linked: a whole chain of monitors shows from one computer. It needs no power of its own; it lights while the computer is on (with SETUP's background services off, only while someone is at the computer).$(br2)Right-click cycles $(thing)LIVE MOSAIC$() (refreshed as lines come in), $(thing)LOOP$() (the last passes, a second each) and $(thing)OFF$().

pages.title: A video wall
pages.text: Monitors facing the same way, edge to edge, make one screen, up to 8 wide and 6 high: the picture runs across them all, hidden behind the bezels between the tubes as on a real video wall. Break one and the wall splits into smaller screens.$(br2)It is an old tube: scanlines, a little flicker, a hum bar now and then.

pages.title: A radio's waterfall
pages.text: Put a single monitor touching a $(thing)premium$() radio (one built with a Pure crystal: the premium HF rigs or the premium VHF base station; not a plain or cheap one) and it shows a waterfall round the radio's dial, as rig control's does but zoomed in: signals scroll down, faint blue to bright white.$(br2)Right-click cycles $(thing)NARROW$(), $(thing)WIDE$() and $(thing)OFF$(). It lights while the radio is on.

pages.title: How wide
pages.text: On HF and CB, NARROW is 6 kHz (one voice and its neighbours, or a few CW signals) and WIDE 24 kHz. On VHF, NARROW is 50 kHz (an FM channel and those either side) and WIDE 200 kHz. Near a band edge the span slides to stay in the band.$(br2)A WXSAT computer beside it wins, and a monitor that is part of a bigger screen never shows a radio.
Iron round a glass pane, over wire and a copper ingot.
